evidence: Scan leaf 17 at 400 dpi, full page, three enlarged bands and enlarged power-image detail: The invoked 2.1(ii) requires geometric normality. Explicitly, in characteristic 3 take k=F_3(a) and the plane cubic y^2 z=x^3+a z^3. Its sole nonsmooth closed point has maximal ideal generated by y and the point at infinity is smooth, so this proper curve is regular. After adjoining a cube root of a it is a cuspidal cubic, whose connected Picard group is G_a, by the normalization-unit quotient. Thus ordinary normality does not make Pic^0 proper or abelian. This confirms the existing geometric-normality qualification.
